root_idea.summary: The root branches around three related principles: inarticulate or unintelligible speech, hardness and resistance, and biting or testing by contact with the teeth.
root_idea.development: From biting and testing come meanings of examining, proving, and being found hard or hardy; from speech that is not understood come meanings of inarticulacy, foreignness, silence, and obscurity. The marking of writing with dots is also explained as an impressed sign that makes otherwise unclear letters distinguishable.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular citation form أَعْجَمِيّ.
أَعْجَمِينَ is the Quranic plural inflection of the same lexical item and is represented under أَعْجَمِيّ.

senses.definition: A non-Arab or foreigner; one belonging to non-Arab peoples.
senses.usage_conditions: Used substantivally of a person or people in contrast with Arabs. The plural أَعْجَمِينَ has this sense in the Quran.

senses.definition: Foreign or non-Arabic, especially of a language or speech.
senses.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally with language, speech, or a Quran described as not Arabic; the construction contrasts foreign speech with clear Arabic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bite or chew something, especially with the lateral teeth; also to bite an object in order to test its hardness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be food, wood, a stick, a rod, or a gaming arrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To try, test, examine, or prove a person, object, or matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: By extension, affairs may test and inure a person, and an object may be examined through biting or other physical trial.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the eye to seem to recognize someone without identifying him with certainty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for uncertain recognition or a sense that one has seen someone before.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fail to determine or recognize the letters of a written text.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of looking into a book or writing without being sure of its letters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make speech, language, or expression unclear, inarticulate, or lacking correctness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the making of speech difficult to understand, as opposed to marking writing so that its letters become distinguishable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dot or diacritically mark a letter or writing so as to remove its ambiguity and distinguish it from similar letters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to the use of dots and related signs in writing; the marking clarifies the script rather than making speech unclear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lock a door.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate conventional use of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cook date-stones until they become as though chewed or bitten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the reported expression concerning cooking date-stones too intensely and thereby spoiling their useful strength or taste.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become silent, speechless, or unable to speak; of a place, to give no answer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be used of a person, a dwelling, or another source of response that remains silent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For speech or recitation to become impeded, closed off, or impossible to continue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of being tongue-tied or unable to continue reading or reciting, including when drowsiness interrupts recitation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For information or a report to become obscure, confused, vague, or difficult to understand or express.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The information is treated as though it were closed against the speaker or hearer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Young camels, both male and female, before they enter the later age category.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun for specified young-camel age classes; the plural is عُجُومٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The root or base of the tail, the coccyx.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal variant of عَجْبٌ according to the cited lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Foreigners, especially people who are not Arabs; the non-Arab peoples collectively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can refer particularly to Persians and may be used without implying that the person speaks Arabic poorly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The stones, pits, or kernels of dates, grapes, raisins, pomegranates, lote-fruits, and similar things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular is عَجَمَةٌ; the meaning may extend to the hard inner part of an edible thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels that bite or chew thorn trees and thereby satisfy themselves without other fodder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive use applied to camels feeding on thorny vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hard rock protruding in a valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is عَجَمَاتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Impediment, difficulty, or lack of clarity and correctness in speech, especially in speaking Arabic.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes the condition of inarticulate or non-perspicuous utterance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An accumulation or elevation of sand, including the last portion of sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may denote sand congested together or rising above the surrounding ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A palm-tree growing from a date-stone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun connected with the date-stone meaning of عَجَمٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intelligent and discriminating.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the separately vocalized adjective with a quiescent ج and is not the nisba meaning “of the non-Arabs.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of or belonging to the non-Arabs; foreign in relation to the Arabs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nisba adjective that may be applied to a person or thing associated with the عَجَم.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Speech or a language foreign to the Arabs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes foreign speech or language, without necessarily asserting that it is unintelligible.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing that has been bitten or chewed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun formed from the act of biting or chewing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large bat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The teeth; by extension, camels that bite or chew bones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural noun is explained through the biting action of the teeth and the camels to which the action is attributed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strong she-camel, especially one strong and enduring enough for travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may describe strength in the animal itself or strength for undertaking a journey.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person whose speech is impeded, unclear, or inarticulate, especially in Arabic.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The person may be Arab or non-Arab; the defining feature is the speech difficulty, not ethnic origin. The adjective may also describe speech, a tongue, or writing that lacks clarity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dumb, speechless, or destitute of the faculty of speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person or other being unable to speak; the feminine form عَجْمَاءُ can become a substantive for a brute animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beast or brute animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized feminine form, explained by the animal's inability to speak.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stallion camel whose braying does not issue from its faucial sac.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a camel whose vocal sac has no opening through which the sound can emerge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A daytime prayer in which Quran recitation is inaudible.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional designation for the noon and afternoon prayers, referring to their non-vocalized recitation; it is not a Quranic verse citation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Waves that neither sprinkle their water nor produce an audible sound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative descriptive expression for unusually quiet or non-splashing waves.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tract of sand in which there are no trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized landscape description reported as an assumed figurative extension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Barbarous, defective, or otherwise non-chaste speech or language.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This usage emphasizes faulty or uncultivated expression rather than merely its being foreign.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mighty, strong, resistant, or indomitable when tested by affairs or events.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person of hardy spirit and, in a related expression, to a she-camel with strength and endurance for crossing the desert.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The letters of the alphabet, especially the letters of a dotted script that are distinguished from one another by their points.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is associated with the Arabic writing system and with the process of making letters distinguishable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Locked, when applied to a door.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate passive-participial use from the lexical discussion of Form IV.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plant or herbage much bitten or eaten, with little remaining.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of vegetation heavily grazed or consumed.

cautions: أَعْجَمِيّ in the Quranic form is used for non-Arab persons or foreign/non-Arabic language; the separate classical adjective أَعْجَمُ primarily concerns inarticulate or unintelligible speech, while عَجَمِيّ is a nisba to non-Arab peoples.
The reported classical designation صَلَاةٌ عَجْمَاءُ refers to inaudible daytime Quran recitation and is not a modern Quran verse citation.
